# ANALYSIS: RSI_OVERSOLD_FILTER_CONTRIBUTION

**Filed:** 2026-07-21
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** filter_change
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The RSI‑oversold filter is intended to improve the quality of bearish entries by avoiding trades in overbought conditions. We hypothesize that the filter currently contributes positively to edge_capture by skipping low-quality bearish setups that would otherwise lose, while preserving the winning bearish trades on J's anchor days.

## Mechanism

The RSI‑oversold filter (assuming it is a filter that blocks entries when RSI is above a certain threshold, e.g., RSI > 70 for bearish entries) is applied in the entry path for bearish setups. It uses the RSI indicator calculated on the 5-minute chart, with a lookback period of 14 bars, and blocks the entry if the RSI value is above 70 at the time of the trigger bar.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** We assume a $25K+ account size for full qty=28 contracts (as per the OP-20 disclosure requirement). For paper trading, $1K account would realize approximately 14% of the headline P&L due to qty scaling.
2. **Sample bias:** The backtest will be run on the full 16-month OPRA real-fills dataset (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) as used in the leaderboard. This dataset is not subject to selection bias as it is the full available history. However, the RSI‑oversold filter's parameters (if any) are taken from the current engine configuration, which may have been optimized on this same dataset, posing overfit risk.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (we are running a Stage-1 backtest, which is in-sample. We will need to run an out-of-sample test in Stage-2.)
4. **Real-fills:** The backtest will use the grinder harness with real OPRA fills, so we will have real-fills check on the top 3 J days after the backtest. Currently: NEEDS-REAL-FILLS.
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: if the filter causes us to miss a big winner (e.g., 5/04) by incorrectly filtering out a valid bearish setup. Max drawdown: could increase if the filter causes us to take more losers by failing to filter them out. Blow-up scenario: if the filter is too loose and we take many losing trades in a row during a volatile regime.
6. **Concentration:** We do not know what percentage of the P&L comes from the top 5 days without the backtest. We will disclose after the backtest.

## Pre-merge gate

The backtest must pass gym validators (all tests pass), and we must verify that the RSI‑oversold filter is correctly implemented in the grinder harness. We will also run a walk-forward test to check for overfit.
